correctness.rationale: For g>=0 the global quadratic dissipation identity bounds the mean-field drift by negative nearest-neighbor Dirichlet energy; finite-N stationary second/fourth moment bounds ensure the stationary central-limit regime. The OU drift/noise matrices are independently reconstructed from the nonlinear logistic flux, their Fourier eigenvalues and stationary Lyapunov covariance are calculated explicitly, and the integrated covariance produces the finite-M coefficient. Pairing the two endpoint Fourier bands under delta=zeta/M and dominated convergence proves the coth scaling; a bounded angular Riemann sum handles fixed nonzero bias. The embedded independent-matrix and asymptotic checker passed 1,554 assertions. This is not an exact finite-N law or a simultaneous joint limit.

value.rationale: The experimentally observable long-time occupation-average precision cannot be inferred from the known bias-independent static stationary covariance. The exact coefficient is strictly reduced by circulation for every fixed ring, while an explicit hyperbolic-cotangent crossover identifies the sharp asymptotic weak-drive scale delta=Theta(1/M); this is a nontrivial natural spectral/hydrodynamic classification, not an arbitrary finite parameter substitution. The positive-repulsion regime is motivated by global stability, which is proved rather than presumed.
